items.title: Australia's proposed AI safety bill would force frontier model makers to open up to independent testing
items.excerpt: Australia's government, led by Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, wants to enshrine mandatory safety rules for frontier AI companies in law for the first time. A new regulator would enforce independent model audits and impose steep penalties for violations. With this move, Canberra is deliberately prioritizing domestic regulation before entering international talks. items.title: Google Deepmind shifts genomics AI from bulk tissue predictions to single cell type resolution with AlphaGenome 2
items.excerpt: Google Deepmind has unveiled AlphaGenome 2, an AI model that analyzes genetic variants for individual cell types rather than across bulk tissue. Trained on more than 107 million cell profiles, it identifies nearly twice as many disease-relevant gene changes as its predecessor. The model is available for noncommercial research through an API and is set to be integrated into Google's agentic platform Antigravity. items.title: New research could lead to faster, trustworthy AI models for climate prediction
items.excerpt: MIT scientists developed a training method to generate models that simulate the effects of human activities on climate much more quickly than other approaches.

items.title: IBM Announces IBM Quantum Nighthawk r3: A New Processor to Support 10k Quantum Operations on 520 Programmable Qubits
items.excerpt: IBM announced Quantum Nighthawk r3, a 520-qubit processor designed for 10,000 quantum operations. 2 r3 chips will link into a 1,040-qubit system in 2027, while Nighthawk r2 already posts up to 19x speedups over Heron.
